title: ר' שמעון בן יהוצדק

paragraphs: 1. Resh Lakish called him a cattle herder: Zeh Borer. There were two, and one was in R' Tarfon's days. Concerning Yuhasin's statement “one in R' Tarfon's days”: if so, there must have been three; but I wrote that he erred. See what I wrote under R' Tarfon. As to there being two, Tosafot, Niddah, first chapter, 10b, write likewise. “R' Yohanan said in R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name”; they ask, and so forth. But R' Yohanan said, “I do not know whether it is his own or his teacher's.” Tosafot write: it appears from here that R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak was R' Yohanan's teacher. In Zeh Borer, 26a, however, Resh Lakish calls him a cattle herder. Had he been R' Yohanan's teacher, how could R' Yohanan not protest at his calling his teacher a cattle herder before him? Rabbenu Tam says that there were two. End of quotation. Tosafot, Avodah Zarah 59a and Nedarim 10, write likewise. In Sukkah, first chapter, 11b: “R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's words; the sages say.” This suggests that he was early, since the sages disagree with him. Tosafot likewise write that R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak was a tanna. Possibly this is the one mentioned in the Talmud, “R' Yohanan said in R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name.” He is not the one in Zeh Borer, whom Resh Lakish called a cattle herder. R' Yohanan told him, “Had he called you sheep herders, what could I do for you?” He would not have answered him thus, but would have protested for his teacher's honor. End of quotation.

2. Yuhasin writes under yod: “R' Yohanan, R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's pupil, in Sanhedrin.” End of quotation. I do not know where in Sanhedrin. If he means the foregoing Zeh Borer, Tosafot proved the contrary from there: because he did not protest for his honor, he was evidently not his teacher; there were two, not one. There is another proof that the one in Zeh Borer was not his teacher: R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak said to R' Yohanan, “Resh Lakish called us cattle herders, and the master said nothing to him!” Had R' Yohanan been his pupil, how could he call his pupil R' Yohanan “master”? Moreover, how could he answer, “If he called you sheep herders, what could I say?” Why should R' Yohanan add disgrace to disgrace? Silence as assent would have sufficed.

But as to Tosafot's statement in Niddah that he appears to have been R' Yohanan's teacher because it says, “I do not know whether his own or his teacher's”: see a contradiction to their words. In Bava Batra 116a, R' Yohanan said in R' Shimon ben Yohai's name, and it says there, “This is his own; that is his teacher's.” So too in Eruvin 64b and Pesahim 26b. R' Yohanan was not R' Shimon ben Yohai's pupil, for R' Yohanan was young in Rabbi's time, and Rabbi was R' Shimon ben Yohai's pupil. In Yoma 3b: did R' Yohanan say this? But he said in R' Yishmael's name, and so forth; it resolves, “This is his own; that is his teacher's.” Certainly R' Yohanan did not see R' Yishmael, who preceded him by much. How, then, did Tosafot prove from “or his teacher's” concerning R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak that he was R' Yohanan's teacher? Although it proves that he was earlier than R' Yohanan, it does not necessarily mean that R' Yohanan was his pupil. A clearer proof that R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak was his teacher is Yoma 43b: “R' Yohanan does not heed even his teacher R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak.” It is also puzzling why Tosafot did not explain this in Rosh Hashanah 34, beginning of side b; Yoma 22 end of side b, 43b; Sukkah 27a; Pesahim 95b; Ta'anit 28b; Ketubbot 72b; Nedarim 45a. It asks, “Did R' Yohanan say this? But he said in R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name …,” and resolves, “This is his own; that is his teacher's.” They should have commented there that this suggests R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak was R' Yohanan's teacher. Why did they wait to explain themselves until Niddah?

Another proof is the earlier authorities' statement—see the rules in the introduction—that wherever it says “so-and-so in so-and-so's name,” he is his pupil. In Arakhin 10a; Sukkah 27a; Sanhedrin 90b; Avodah Zarah 36b, it says “R' Yohanan said in R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name,” as also in many of the foregoing places. In Bava Metzia 22b, “R' Yohanan said in R' Yishmael bar Yehotzadak's name”; in that matter there, 27a, in R' Shimon ben Yohai's name. It appears that both places have scribal errors and should read “in R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's name.” Afterward I found it thus twice in Yalkut, Ki Tetze, remez 1030 [the checked parallel is at remez 930:8], and it pleased me. בשס״ח [provisionally: in the new Talmud editions; uncollated] they did not correct either place.

3. R' Hiyya bar Zarnuki went with him to intercalate years; see his entry. R' Yohanan asked R' Yannai before R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak's bier: Jerusalem Nazir 7:1. Ulla reports in his name: Ta'anit 22b; Menahot 69b. He said to R' Shmuel bar Nahmani, “You are a master of aggadah; from where was light created?”: Bereshit Rabbah, chapter 3; Vayakhel, beginning of chapter 50; Emor, chapter 31. We find R' Shmuel bar Nahmani often reporting in R' Yohanan's name; see his entry. How could R' Yohanan's teacher ask a pupil of his pupil? Thus there must have been two. R' Shimon ben Elazar reports in his name, and he was R' Meir's pupil. Thus R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak must have been early and there were two, though this does not prove that he was R' Yohanan's teacher.
